segments.name: Flexible friends planning a cheap escape
Flexible couple seeking a cheap short break

population.allocation: At least one per positive stratum, then largest remainder; individual estimate weight = target segment share / stratum sample count.

sources.title: Cathay Pacific Annual Report 2025 — HK Express operations
sources.supports: Low-cost leisure positioning, Asian destinations and aggregate passenger statistics; not the assumed target-segment weights.

sources.title: Cathay Group December 2025 traffic figures
sources.supports: Aggregate HK Express passenger counts and load factors; no matching membership conversion or segment-share table.

limitations: The reviewed official reports do not publish these customer distributions; all numerical segment weights and budget distributions remain test assumptions.
This is a deliberately targeted audience for flexible bargain travel, not a representative sample of all HK Express passengers. Fixed-date mandatory, urgent and business travel are excluded.
All sampled travellers are already valid members; no membership purchase, renewal, taxes, fuel fees or airline costs enter this experiment.
Each sampled member decides about one personal ticket; companions' purchases are outside this experiment.
Optional-trip interest, recent travel, destination appeal and the appeal of skipping are pre-price private scenario traits, not observed preferences or numerical willingness-to-pay labels.
Poststratified rates and expected revenue are estimates. Accepted ticket counts and cash revenue remain integer transactions in the cleared panel.
An LLM persona is not an independent observed HK Express customer; repeated choices do not create additional people.

rounds.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

decision.reason: The 496 member fare is a genuinely cheap escape and fits my 547 budget, and friends are flexible on dates and destination. I am keen for an optional break after six months without leisure travel, and this departure is usable. Busan itself is only mildly appealing, but at this price the bargain-led trip is worthwhile; I would not pay the 620 normal fare.

person.eligibility_reason: This optional leisure departure fits the flexible travel window.
person.travel_party_context: Any companions can use this departure and independently arrange and fund their own tickets; this decision covers one existing member only.
person.booking_trigger: Friends have agreed to be flexible about dates and destination if a cheap escape appears; nobody is obliged to make the trip.
person.departure_time_tolerance: Can adapt to the displayed departure time for a worthwhile deal; no fixed appointment requires this flight.
person.value_context: The group enjoys bargain-led trips and can use this departure. This member chooses and pays only for their own ticket; a weak deal can still be declined.
person.outside_option: Suggest another leisure outing or save for a later trip; do not invent a quoted alternative fare.
person.motivation_context: Keen to arrange an optional break, with no ticket booked and no compulsory date or destination. Has not taken a leisure trip in the last six months. This destination is acceptable but has little particular attraction today. Skipping remains possible, though arranging a worthwhile leisure break is preferred.

analysis.summary: Of 16 members, 4 bought the 496 HKD member fare and 12 declined. Nine declines were environment-forced (no ticket both available and within budget), which is an inventory/availability issue rather than a price objection. Three declines cited low trip or destination interest with optional leisure, not fare level. Buyers were strongly price-sensitive and said they would not pay the 620 normal fare. The current fare is at its permitted cap, so no higher test is allowed.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing the same 496 fare on fresh members will reproduce roughly one-quarter member conversion, with declines dominated by availability constraints rather than fare objections; a materially lower conversion would contradict this.

initial_result.accounting: Base ticket receipts only; no membership fee, tax, fuel surcharge or operating costs.

analysis.summary: At the current 222 HKD member fare, 13 of 16 customers bought and 3 declined. All three declines cite low trip interest and a preference to keep schedule and money, not the fare itself. Buyers repeatedly describe 222 as a bargain below their stated ceilings, and several say they would not pay the 620 regular fare. No inventory denials occurred and quota is far from binding. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at today's fare does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases that basic ticket receipts exceed those at 222 HKD; if conversion falls sharply enough to reduce receipts, the higher-fare direction is contradicted.

analysis.summary: At the current 335 HKD member fare, 9 of 16 customers bought, generating 3015 HKD in basic receipts. Most buyers cite the fare as a compelling bargain versus the 620 HKD regular fare, and several would decline at regular price. Four declines are environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and three are low-interest optional browsing rather than price objections. No customer objects primarily to the fare itself. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying at 335 does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough purchases to keep basic ticket receipts at least as high as at 335 HKD, because most current buyers cite the fare as a bargain well below their stated budgets.

analysis.summary: Of 16 members, 5 bought the 477 HKD member fare and 11 declined. Eight declines were inventory/budget-forced (ENVIRONMENT_FORCED), not price objections; three cited low interest or destination appeal, and one cited low appeal plus a recent trip. No customer explicitly objected to the fare level. Buyers valued the 143 HKD saving but several said they would not pay the 620 HKD normal fare. Evidence is mixed and largely non-price, so a directional price test is weakly supported.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a lower member fare on fresh members will not meaningfully raise conversion, because most declines stem from unavailable inventory or low trip interest rather than fare level; conversion should stay within a few points of the current rate.

analysis.summary: At the current 340 HKD member fare, six members bought and ten declined. Among decliners, five cited low trip interest or a preferred free schedule (other), and five were blocked by unavailable inventory within budget (availability). No customer objected to the fare itself; buyers called it a bargain, and one would even pay the 620 regular fare. The paired initial at 496 HKD produced far fewer buyers and lower revenue, but that comparison is not a fresh test. Evidence points to testing a higher fare rather than lowering it.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce basic-ticket receipts versus 340 HKD, because current buyers describe the fare as a bargain and one accepts the 620 regular fare. A revenue drop or conversion collapse would contradict this.

analysis.summary: At the current 362 HKD member fare, 4 of 16 members bought, citing strong value versus the 620 HKD normal fare. Six declines were inventory/budget-forced (no available ticket within budget), and five declines were low trip interest or optional-leisure preference, not price objections. No customer objected to the fare itself as too high. Evidence points to availability and trip motivation, not fare level, as the main conversion barriers.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce weighted conversion materially because buyers cite value versus the 620 HKD normal fare and no decline cites price; if conversion falls sharply, the hypothesis is contradicted.

analysis.summary: At the current 316 HKD member fare, 8 of 16 customers bought, all citing the low fare as decisive and all rejecting the 620 HKD fallback. Four declines were inventory/budget-forced, and four were optional-trip or destination-interest objections where price was already affordable. No customer objected to price itself. The paired initial at the 496 HKD cap produced fewer buyers and lower revenue, suggesting the low fare drives conversion. Evidence supports testing a higher fare on fresh customers, though buying today does not prove willingness to pay more.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will retain enough buyers that basic ticket receipts meet or exceed those at 316 HKD; if conversion falls sharply and receipts drop, the low-fare dependence is confirmed.

proposal.capacity_model: exact Binomial capacity expectation for iid weighted target cohort
proposal.uncertainty_kind: model mean-revenue percentiles, not realized-revenue or validated human intervals

limitations: Synthetic choice response, not calibrated human demand.
Repeated choices are tempered by persona; the posterior is not an exact independent-observation posterior.
Gaussian local approximation and proper priors remain influential for small panels.

analysis.summary: At the 339 HKD member fare, 7 of 16 customers bought and 9 declined. Among decliners, five cite low trip interest or recent travel, and four cite no available ticket within budget; none primarily objects to the fare itself. Buyers repeatedly describe 339 as a bargain and several say they would refuse the 620 regular fare. The evidence points to voluntary-trip motivation and inventory, not price, as the main barriers, so a fare cut is not clearly supported.
analysis.hypothesis: Testing a higher member fare on fresh customers will not reduce member conversion enough to lower basic receipts, because current buyers cite the fare as a bargain and declines stem from low trip interest or unavailable inventory rather than price.

analysis.summary: At the current 300 HKD member fare, 11 of 16 customers bought, generating 3300 HKD in basic receipts, while 5 declined. Most buyers explicitly cite the low fare as the decisive trigger and say they would not pay the 620 HKD normal fare. Three declines are environment-forced (no available ticket within budget), and two are low-interest browsers for whom price was not the objection. The evidence points to strong price sensitivity, so testing a higher fare risks losing conversions.
analysis.hypothesis: Raising the member fare above 300 HKD will reduce member conversion enough that basic ticket receipts fall, because most current buyers describe the low fare as the decisive purchase trigger rather than destination appeal.

assumptions: Only existing members; no joining or renewal decision and no fee deduction.
Base fares only; all taxes/fuel/add-ons and operating costs excluded. Revenue is not airline profit.
Population weights are explicit scenario assumptions, not measured HK Express market shares.
Fresh stratified members each search round; paired candidate and initial quote in reset, blinded worlds. One seat per member per world.
Only declared public segment/flexibility enter learning; private budgets, motivation and simulator constraints remain environment-only.
Every third round may test a cited LLM direction within a bounded model-scored interval; text never adds a demand label.
Analyst requests allow at most three attempts within the shared call budget. Unavailable analysis supplies no direction; recorded purchases still train Thompson and undergo independent confirmation.
Quoted fares are whole HKD; weighted averages and statistical estimates may have decimals.
Parallel intent elicitation followed by fixed-priority integer inventory clearing; no seat is reserved by an LLM.
Weighted demand estimates and actual panel cash/seat transactions are reported separately.
Final member quotes round down to an amount ending in nine, with any result below HK$30 becoming HK$0; raw search prices remain recorded.
Independent validation compares the formatted initial fallback, formatted selected fare and no offer after freezing both final quotes; no refitting on holdout.
